title: reduce-gpu-memory-activation-checkpointing-arena-tuning-scratch-buffers-and-batching
author: Ava Chen
description: Context: High-memory GPU inference runs (8k+ context, large batch windows) were hitting workspace limits on NGC/tenant deployments. This PR reduces device memory and transient workspace usage via: 1) follow-up activation checkpointing for multi-layer transformer blocks with configurable checkpoint granularity; 2) reworking the arena allocator to prefer compact scratch regions and reuse transient buffers across attention/kernels; 3) introducing a shared scratch-buffer pool for kernels that previously allocated per-call scratch memory; 4) small scheduling tweaks to continuous batching to avoid pathological peak coalescing that increased temporary allocations. Motivation: enable larger effective batch windows and longer contexts without needing larger reserved GPUs and reduce OOM incidents observed in customer Dedicated clusters. Summary of changes and impact: - Activation checkpointing: new option checkpoint.granularity (layer|block|auto) and a lightweight heuristic that enables block-level checkpointing for models > 7B. Measured ~18-26% reduction in peak model activations for Llama-like architectures. - Arena tuning: changed default allocation strategy from "power-of-two" growth to a hybrid fit-first with limited growth cap; reduces internal fragmentation and peak arena usage by ~12-20% on workloads with mixed sequence lengths. - Scratch buffer pool: consolidated per-kernel scratch allocations into a shared pool with size estimation by kernel family; reduces transient allocations and lowers memory churn, saving ~6-10% peak workspace in benchmarks. - Continuous batching scheduling: minor backoff and batching window smoothing to prevent temporary spikes when multiple large requests arrive simultaneously; yields similar latency P95 with lower peak memory. Testing & benchmarks: included microbenchmarks under tests/perf/bench_gpu_memory.py and end-to-end smoke runs on Dedicated test cluster. On the 24GB GPU baseline test (16x batch of 2048 tokens) we observe a median peak memory reduction of 34% (combined) and negligible impact on token throughput (+1-3% variance). Backwards compatibility: defaults preserve current behavior (checkpointing off; arena aggressive growth off) and require opt-in via runtime config or model profile. Rollout plan: feature-flag gated on Dedicated and Private by default; staged rollout for Hosted with nightly perf runs and monitoring alerts before full enable. Checklist: - [x] unit tests for arena allocator behavior - [x] perf harness for memory benchmarks - [x] integration smoke tests on Dedicated cluster - [x] docs/upgrade notes - [x] Linear tickets updated How to review: focus on the arena allocator changes (runtime/memory/arena_allocator.cpp) and the scratch pool lifetime semantics. CI notes: an earlier CI run failed intermittently on perf.yml due to flaky perf runner; addressed by pinning runner image and retry logic. Merge notes: squash-merge after approvals.
commits: add: activation checkpointing support with configurable granularity
fix: arena allocator fit-first strategy and limited growth cap
feat: shared scratch buffer pool and kernel family estimators
perf: continuous batching scheduling smoothing to reduce transient peaks
test: perf harness and unit tests for allocator and scratch pool
docs: upgrade notes and runtime config examples

release_notes:
- Reduced GPU peak memory via activation checkpointing (configurable) and arena allocator tuning.
- Introduced shared scratch-buffer pool to lower transient workspace usage.
- Minor continuous batching improvements to reduce memory spikes.
Note: features are gated and opt-in by default; see docs/upgrade.md for rollout steps.
additional_notes: This PR was driven by Dedicated cluster OOM incidents in SUP-3142. Customers running >8k contexts should test with checkpoint.granularity=block. Ops: monitor runtime.memory.peak and runtime.scratch_pool.usage metrics after rollout.
